worksheet.title: What Comes Next?
worksheet.subtitle: Reading a pattern that repeats
worksheet.learning_goal: I can read a pattern and draw what comes next.

parts.title: Patterns repeat
parts.text: A pattern is a row that repeats the same way. If you know the pattern, you can tell what comes next.

parts.title: Watch Bit — ▲ ■ ▲ ■ …
parts.note: It goes triangle, square, triangle, square. After ▲ comes ■. The next one is ■.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the pattern out loud, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the pattern, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: You try — a longer pattern
parts.prompt: This pattern goes two-then-one. Read it and draw what comes next.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Reading a pattern lets you know what comes next. Computers follow patterns too — that is how they repeat a job the same way every time.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children read a repeating pattern and identify the next element. Recognizing and continuing patterns is a foundational computational-thinking skill — it is how computers repeat a process the same way every time.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children identify, reproduce, and extend repeating patterns.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child draws the next shape.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil/crayon. Optional: pattern blocks or beads to build the pattern by hand first.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: point and say the pattern aloud — 'triangle, square, triangle, square…'. The next is a square.
2. GUIDED: do Exercise 1 together — read ● ★ ● ★ ● aloud, the next is ★.
3. YOU TRY: children do Exercise 2 (next is ■), then Exercise 3, the two-then-one pattern (next is ★).
4. Connect: 'Computers follow patterns too — that is how they repeat a job exactly the same way.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — ● ★ ● ★ ● → next is ★.   Ex 2 — ■ ▲ ■ ▲ → next is ■.
Ex 3 — ★ ★ ● ★ ★ ● → next is ★ (the pattern is star, star, circle, repeating).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: copying the last shape shown — have them say the whole pattern aloud first.
Simplify: build the pattern with real blocks and add the next one by hand.
Extend: ask the child to keep the pattern going for two or three more shapes.
Movement option: clap–stomp–clap–stomp and ask what action comes next.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child says the repeating unit aloud and draws the correct next shape for each pattern.
